beats.beat: The company operates in two segments: creation of infrastructure and operation of a ready-mix concrete (RMC) plant. The infrastructure work includes railways, bridges, and roads.

Contracts are won through a tender process where the company bids against competitors and is awarded the work as the lowest quote. The client issues a Letter of Acceptance and the company deposits a performance guarantee.

Major clients include Western Railway, Central Railway, Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation (MRVCL), Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM), and Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA). Western Railway has been a client since 2006 and contributed 52% of the order book as of the DRHP date.
The company’s revenue is heavily concentrated: its top customers accounted for 57% of total revenue in fiscal 2018. This dependence on a few government clients is a key risk.

Its competitive strengths, as stated in the DRHP, include long-standing client relationships, use of modern techniques (e.g., box-pushing), experienced management (over 20 years in infrastructure), and a state-of-the-art RMC facility at Kashimira, Thane.
Geographically, the company is focused on Mumbai and is slowly expanding across Maharashtra. It claims a healthy order book.

beats.beat: The restated financials (in ₹ lakhs) show a declining revenue trend: ₹9,021.12 (FY2015) → ₹7,452.76 (FY2016) → ₹7,344.47 (FY2017) → ₹6,053.05 (FY2018). The compound decline reflects, in part, slower government project execution.

Profit after tax (PAT) was volatile: ₹95.95 (FY2014), ₹78.36 (FY2015), ₹32.63 (FY2016), ₹15.86 (FY2017), before spiking to ₹314.66 (FY2018). The sharp increase in FY2018 is notable but not explained in the excerpts.
EBITDA (Profit Before Interest, Depreciation and Tax) shows a similar pattern: ₹784.46 (FY2014), ₹945.78 (FY2015), ₹783.31 (FY2016), ₹676.19 (FY2017), ₹928.80 (FY2018).

Debt levels: long-term borrowings stood at ₹133.09 lakhs as of FY2018, down from ₹586.63 lakhs in FY2014. Short-term borrowings, however, rose to ₹3,537.35 lakhs in FY2018 from ₹3,082.27 lakhs in FY2014 — indicating increased reliance on working capital finance.
The company has reported negative cash flows in recent years, a risk factor that the DRHP acknowledges explicitly.
Key ratios: P/E for FY2018 was 28.14, EPS was ₹12.39, and RoNW was 44.71%. These are as per the DRHP’s own calculation.

beats.beat: Promoter Amit Bholanath Mishra holds 74,95,476 equity shares (90.949% of pre-issue capital). He is also the Managing Director.

The other directors hold only 300 shares each. Key management personnel include CFO Anchal Pachori (aged 28, a CA) and Company Secretary Mohit Soni (aged 26, an ACS). Hatim Sakerwala holds 9% of equity shares.

Related-party transactions: In FY2018, loans taken from KMP/Board of Directors were ₹68.4 lakhs, director remuneration was ₹57.7 lakhs, and outstanding payables to related parties were ₹324.3 lakhs as of 31 March 2018.

Governance flags: Two companies promoted by Amit Mishra — Al-Noor Chickens Pvt. Ltd. and A B Magma Automobiles Pvt. Ltd. — were struck off by the ROC in March 2016 for non-operation. The company also issued equity shares at a price lower than the issue price within the last 12 months.

No independent agency has appraised the project, and no monitoring agency is appointed for fund utilisation. The DRHP states no director is on the RBI list of willful defaulters and no criminal cases are filed against directors.

beats.beat: The infrastructure sector is highly fragmented and working capital intensive, contributing about 8% to India’s GDP at constant prices.
Key growth drivers cited: government flagship programs (Smart Cities, AMRUT, Make in India), eased FDI norms in 15 sectors (including real estate), rising urbanization, and rising disposable income.

India requires an estimated ₹50 trillion (US$777.73 billion) in infrastructure investment by 2022. The logistics sector alone is expected to grow at a CAGR of 10.5% from US$160 billion in 2017 to US$215 billion by 2020.

Headwinds acknowledged in the DRHP: slow pace of government projects, working capital crunches affecting profitability, and changes in government policies. The industry is also subject to regulations under the Companies Act, GST, Factories Act, and environmental laws.
Competition comes from both organized and unorganized players, and the market is described as highly competitive.

beats.beat: A B Infrabuild Limited is an infrastructure construction and ready-mix concrete (RMC) company based in Mumbai, operating primarily on contracts from government entities like Indian Railways and municipal bodies.
It is raising ₹[●] crore through a fresh issue of 44,28,000 equity shares (face value ₹10) on the SME Board of NSE/BSE. The issue is a pure fresh issue with no offer for sale.
The proceeds are earmarked largely for working capital (₹11.30 crore) and general corporate purposes, according to the DRHP.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who this company is, what it does, what it is raising and why it matters

beats.beat: The issue comprises 44,28,000 equity shares of ₹10 each at a price to be determined. It is a fresh issue; there is no offer for sale.
The Lead Manager is Mark Corporate Advisors Private Limited and the Registrar is Bigshare Services Private Limited.

Proceeds from the issue: ₹11.30 crore (1,130 lakhs) is allocated to meet working capital requirements. The remainder is for general corporate purposes; the exact amount is not disclosed (marked [●] in the DRHP).
The company has not appointed an independent agency to appraise the project, and no monitoring agency has been appointed — fund deployment will be monitored by the Audit Committee.

beats.beat: Customer concentration: Western Railway contributed 52% of the order book and 57% of fiscal 2018 revenue. Loss of this client would cause a significant revenue dip.
Negative cash flows: The company has sustained negative cash flows in recent years, which could impair its ability to meet working capital needs or service debt.
Pending litigation: The company, promoter, and directors are involved in litigation that could result in liabilities and penalties if decided adversely.
Order book cancellations: Contracts in the order book may be adjusted, cancelled, or suspended by clients, so the order book does not guarantee future revenue.
Repayable unsecured loans: As of March 31, 2018, unsecured loans of ₹405.02 lakhs are repayable on demand. Any demand for repayment could strain cash flow.

beats.beat: The DRHP includes a table ‘Comparison of Accounting Ratios with Peer Group Companies’ but does not name the peer companies in the extracted facts. The available data shows EPS of 12.39, NAV per share of 44.71, and RoNW of 28.14 (FY2018). No peer names or their multiples are provided.

The issue price has not been determined (shown as [●] in the DRHP). The DRHP states that the price will be justified based on the accounting ratios, but no implicit price range can be calculated due to the absence of peer multiples.
Given the lack of named peers, an implied price range from peer comparison is not possible. Investors must rely on the company’s own financials and market conditions when the price is fixed.
